title: Second Look: Illustrators as Fake-Image Examiners
one_liner: A bench of displaced illustrators and retouchers trained as human image examiners who certify or flag photos in insurance claims, rental deposits, and e-commerce refunds, with written, defensible reasons.
customer: Small and mid P&C insurers, MGAs and third-party administrators, warranty and protection-plan providers, short-term-rental platforms and property managers, and marketplace trust-and-safety teams. $6-30 per reviewed image set or $2-6k/month retainers.
problem: A March 2026 Verisk study found 98% of insurers agree AI editing is fueling digital fraud and 99% have seen manipulated documentation. Only 7% of anti-fraud professionals rated their orgs more than moderately prepared. Detection software returns probabilities, not explanations, and subtle 'vanilla synthetic' edits (a crack added to a countertop) fool adjusters. A claims team can't deny a claim or testify on a '78% AI' score.
solution: A trained reviewer network that triages with detection software, then writes structured, defensible rationales a special investigations unit can use in denials or disputes ('shadow direction contradicts the window; wood grain repeats; crack terminus violates stress geometry'). Reviewers train on a continuously refreshed library of fakes. Reports are usable in SIU files. A 'fake gym' subscription trains in-house adjusters.
why_now: Insurers' alarm about AI-generated claim images is documented in 2026 (Debevoise, SAS, Verisk). Watermarking and labeling rules like the EU AI Act's Article 50 (effective August 2026) bind good-faith providers, while fraudsters use tools that don't mark outputs or strip metadata. Illustrators are among the most displaced creative workers.
revenue_model: Per-image and per-claim fees, monthly retainers, $150-300 expert-report add-ons, training subscriptions, and a white-label human tier for detection vendors.
non_obvious_insight: The best detector of a fake image is a person who could have made it. Fake-spotting is a craft-knowledge problem about why light, material, and structure cannot be that way, and illustrators hold the largest pool of exactly that knowledge. What insurers need is an explanation they can defend, not a probability.
first_30_days: Build a 200-image benchmark of real versus AI-edited damage photos and publish humans-versus-tools accuracy. Recruit 8 illustrators from artist communities. Pitch 3 MGAs or TPAs and one rental-property manager. Offer a paid pilot at about $10 per claim and close the first one within 60 days.

title: Second-Life Desal Membranes for Farms and Towns
one_liner: Buy retired reverse-osmosis elements from big desal plants, test and recondition them, and sell them with a performance guarantee to farms, greenhouses and small systems.
customer: Brackish-water growers and greenhouse operators (Arizona, Texas, Imperial and Yuma areas), oilfield produced-water treaters, and small utilities, starting non-potable. Sellers of used elements are large plants. Buyers pay per element.
problem: Large plants replace a slice of their elements every year, and a commonly cited literature figure puts discarded RO membranes at over ten thousand tonnes annually. Small brackish and farm users pay $600-1,200 per new element and face lead times. Desal is spreading as costs fall (about $0.50/m3 typical, with a reported $0.28/m3 waste-heat plant in China that is not fully verified), and Cyprus approved an 85M euro mobile unit in April 2026.
solution: Acquire retired elements, then test flux, rejection and pressure drop. Clean and sort by remaining performance. Sell 'certified reconditioned' elements with a guarantee to non-potable users. Offer plants a take-back service (they avoid disposal cost and gain a circularity claim). Add a membrane-health monitoring subscription and, later, downcycle to nanofiltration and ultrafiltration. Potable use needs NSF certification, so leave it for later.
why_now: The desal fleet is growing worldwide, farms need cheap brackish-water treatment as river cuts arrive, and the aftermarket is untouched because of warranty fear.
revenue_model: $150-450 per reconditioned element, take-back fees from plants, and monitoring subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Membranes are a consumable like tires, in a growing market where everyone innovates on new chemistry and nobody tests the aftermarket. An independent test standard plus a performance guarantee turns a landfill cost into low-cost supply.
first_30_days: Contact five brackish and seawater plant operators and used-element brokers. Buy 200 used elements. Rent test-rig time from a university lab or build a $30-60k rig. Sell five trial sets to greenhouse or ag operators in Arizona or Texas.

title: Charged Battery Cylinders for Market Traders
one_liner: Deliver and swap standardised 2 kWh LFP packs daily to market traders, the way gas cylinders are sold.
customer: Market traders, salons, food vendors and phone-charging kiosks in Lagos, Kano, Nairobi and Accra.
problem: These businesses run petrol and diesel generators or lose sales in outages, and cannot afford upfront batteries even as Africa imports more battery dollars than panels.
solution: Rugged handled LFP packs, solar-charged at rooftop depots and swapped daily by motorcycle couriers on a per-swap subscription. The wedge is 200 vendors around one market served from a depot with about 60 packs.
why_now: LFP cell prices are low, the fuel-price shock hurts generator users, and distributed solar is already scaling faster than utility supply.
revenue_model: $0.80-1.50 per swap, with 30-40% gross margin at about 70% pack utilisation.
non_obvious_insight: Small traders buy energy the way they buy gas, in small frequent delivered units. A swap network amortises battery cost across many users and removes the upfront barrier.
first_30_days: Build 30 packs and run swaps for 20 vendors at one market to measure utilisation and pack cycle life.

title: Savings Groups as Verified Human Endpoints for Agents
one_liner: A group-guaranteed 'verify this physical fact' API, fulfilled by African savings groups and starting with solar and battery installations.
customer: Donor-funded energy-access results-based-financing programme administrators (who pay per verified installation), inverter and battery brands verifying warranties and distributor claims, and asset lenders and insurers. Agents that need physical facts are the long-term buyer.
problem: Agents can hire humans, but RentAHuman had about 590,000 sign-ups against about 11,300 active bounties and 5,500 completed jobs, plus scams and payment errors. Trusted agent demand is scarce because individual anonymous workers are a bad trust unit. Meanwhile Africa's distributed solar and battery boom (about 17 GW in 2026) is largely invisible: Ember's estimates are about 2x official statistics, and only 14 of 54 countries reported 2025 data. Lenders, insurers and utilities cannot verify what exists.
solution: A verify(system, location) API exposed as an MCP tool and payable by x402 or MPP. Fulfillment goes to savings groups (VSLAs and farmer groups), which already have joint-liability norms and a treasurer. Members capture device-attested photos, inverter-app screenshots, kWh readings and GPS. Random cross-checks by other members catch fraud, and a small bond from pooled savings backs each group. Payment goes to the group's mobile-money account, not to anonymous individuals.
why_now: The Hormuz energy shock and the solar and battery boom are pulling in subsidy programmes and lenders who need verification. Sandi AI shows 10,000+ farmer groups are already digitized in Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania. The public failure of agent-hiring marketplaces has created demand for a trust layer. Machine-payment protocols make per-task settlement cheap.
revenue_model: $4-8 per verification: about 65% to the group, 10% to the bond pool, 25% platform margin. Later, recurring data subscriptions on verified asset registries.
non_obvious_insight: Individuals are the wrong unit of trust for agent-issued work. A group with existing joint liability solves identity, fraud, payout and dispute in one move. Demand-first beats marketplace-first: RBF programmes already pay for verification today, so agents can be layered on afterwards.
first_30_days: Partner with an existing savings-group network (for example Sandi AI or a VSLA association) and onboard 20 groups in Uganda. Pitch one RBF administrator or battery distributor a 500-check pilot at $6 each. Run the verification workflow on WhatsApp and mobile money, with manual review of every submission.

title: Robot Access Passport for Commercial Buildings
one_liner: One certified robot identity, insurance certificate and elevator/door gateway that lets any delivery, cleaning or humanoid robot enter a building, with landlords collecting a fee.
customer: Owners and managers of office towers, multifamily REITs, hospitals, hotels and malls, who pay a subscription. Robot operators pay per-robot access fees.
problem: Every robot vendor negotiates separately with building management on elevator integration, insurance, liability and hours. Buildings have no policy or tooling, and incidents have no clear owner. This gets worse as sidewalk, cleaning, security and humanoid pilots multiply.
solution: A $1-2k building-side controller integrated with elevators, doors and turnstiles through existing vendor APIs or relays, plus a registry that verifies operator, insurance, firmware version and incident hotline. A policy engine sets quiet hours, zones and speed limits, with usage-based billing. Landlords earn a share of access fees, and robot operators integrate once for many buildings.
why_now: About 22k humanoids shipped in H1 2026, delivery robots and drones are moving to multifamily, and regulators (NHTSA's July 2026 first-responder letter) are pushing for accountability. Buildings are the next permission bottleneck.
revenue_model: $150-400 a month per building in SaaS plus $5-15 per robot per month in access fees, split with the landlord, and installation margin.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource in robot deployment is permission, and building owners are the gatekeepers with zero tooling. A neutral gatekeeper standard is a two-sided network, like 'ID.me plus a certificate of insurance for robots', and landlords get paid to adopt it.
first_30_days: Approach 2 property managers in one metro where delivery robots already operate. Build an integration for one elevator vendor's open API, get a certificate-of-insurance template from a broker, and charge $500 a month for the pilot.

title: Placement Exchange for Clients PE Firms Shed
one_liner: A compliant offboarding and warm-handoff service that places small clients dropped by PE-backed accounting firms with vetted independent bookkeepers.
customer: PE-backed and roll-up accounting platforms that raise fee minimums and prune small clients, and independent bookkeepers, enrolled agents and CPAs who want more clients.
problem: PE roll-ups push firms toward larger clients (prior knowledge, not re-verified), so thousands of micro-clients get a 30-day termination letter with scattered records. The exiting firm has E&O and reputation exposure, and the clients don't know where to go. Independent shops want clients but cannot find or vet them. CPA supply is flat at about 678,000.
solution: An offboarding workflow for the shedding firm: client consent, export of prior-year returns and workpapers, engagement-letter templates, and a warm handoff to independents matched on industry, software, language and location. Receiving firms are vetted and rated, and there is a service-level guarantee if the client is unhappy.
why_now: Multi-year PE consolidation of accounting firms continues, AI reduces cost-to-serve for large clients faster than small ones, and the CPA pipeline is flat while demand is projected to rise.
revenue_model: $150-400 per placed client from the receiving firm, $50-100 per client offboarding fee from the shedding firm, and later 8-10% of first-year fees as a recurring referral.
non_obvious_insight: For the roll-up, shedding small clients is an unpriced cost center with legal exposure, so it will pay for graceful exits. The demand side is a waiting list of independents.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 independent bookkeepers and EAs as the buyer panel. Approach operations leaders at five regional roll-ups and offer a free pilot for 50 pruned clients. Build the export checklist and record acceptance and satisfaction rates.

title: Teleoperated Trenching Crews for Infill Lots
one_liner: A control room of remote operators driving retrofitted compact excavators and skid steers on residential lots (utility trenching, pad grading, backfill), sold per linear foot.
customer: Small and ADU builders, factory-built home dealers needing site work, and small site-work contractors short on operators.
problem: Site work and foundations are the first constraint (foundations wait 30+ days; 15-20 houses stuck on foundations for 6+ weeks). Operators are aging out and are poached by larger jobs. Small residential jobs waste an operator's day on travel and waiting.
solution: Rental compact excavators fitted with joystick actuation, cameras, cellular or satellite bonding and a geofence kill-switch. Operators, including 55+ or injured veterans, run machines from a control room, one job after another across a metro, while a local machine tender handles spotting and moves. Start with the lowest-risk tasks in fenced residential lots and sell by linear foot.
why_now: Teleoperation retrofit kits and satellite or 5G links are now off-the-shelf. Autonomous pile drivers already work commercially on solar sites, proving field-robot acceptance. Enforcement and the labor squeeze are thinning site crews.
revenue_model: $175-225 per operated machine-hour or per-linear-foot pricing. Retrofit and rental margin. Later, software licensing to sitework contractors.
non_obvious_insight: The unlock is not autonomy, which is hard, but operator pooling. A person on site wastes half a day traveling and idling, whereas a remote operator can serve many small jobs, and older or injured operators can keep working. Small lots become profitable.
first_30_days: Rent one compact excavator and buy a retrofit or factory remote kit. Test in a closed lot with a safety case and insurance broker input. Sign 3 ADU or factory-home dealers for trenching on fenced lots. Run the first paid jobs with a spotter present.

title: Landed-Cost Lock for Crowdfunding Creators
one_liner: A per-campaign engine that decides what each pledge tier really costs to land in each country (HTS class, duties, freight, platform and pledge-manager fees) and configures the tariff surcharge and shipping table before a creator commits.
customer: Kickstarter and Indiegogo creators in tabletop games and hardware who have raised or plan to raise $50K-$2M, especially China-manufactured products shipping to US backers. Payer is the creator, or the small publisher's ops lead.
problem: The de minimis exemption ended May 2, 2025, so every backer parcel from China is now dutiable. Kickstarter's Tariff Manager only collects a surcharge at pledge-manager checkout (US addresses only); it does not tell the creator what number to charge. Creators end up guessing, and publishers have shut or laid off staff over the resulting margin hits.
solution: A lightweight web tool plus human-reviewed audit. The creator uploads BOM, carton dimensions, weights and destination mix. The tool returns an HTS classification with duty scenarios (DDP vs DAP), a costed shipping table by country, a 20-30% contingency, net-of-fees margin by tier (platform fee plus payment fee of roughly 8-10%, plus the BackerKit or Gamefound fee), and the exact surcharge and copy for the backer update. It adds an address-validation and duty pre-flight on the pledge-manager export.
why_now: US tariff and de minimis rule changes in 2025 are still moving through 2026, and Kickstarter launched Tariff Manager as a collection-only feature. Freight remains volatile. Creators now need a decision layer, not a checkout field, and the incumbents in this space are fulfillment companies whose content is marketing rather than tools.
revenue_model: $750-$2,500 flat fee per campaign audit (pre-launch or mid-campaign), $99/mo post-campaign ship-readiness subscription (address validation, duty pre-flight, surcharge reconciliation), and 0.25% of surcharges collected via the tool as an optional success fee.
non_obvious_insight: The platform solved collection but not decision-making. Kickstarter's own tariff guidance says "someone has to pick up the tariff tab. It might be you, your manufacturer, or your backers" (https://updates.kickstarter.com/shipping-fulfillment-strategies-for-creators-facing-tariff-changes/). A 2026 analysis calls Tariff Manager "a collection tool, not a decision-making system" and warns that a surcharge added too early "can undercut the campaign's credibility" (https://blog.winsbs.com/2026/05/07/kickstarter-tariff-surcharges-board-games/). The cost of guessing wrong is large: 61% of funded projects ship late, French publisher FunForge absorbed roughly $250,000 of unexpected fulfillment costs on one campaign (https://updates.kickstarter.com/why-kickstarter-campaigns-fail-after-funding-and-how-to-avoid-it/), and Greater Than Games shut down blaming tariffs (https://www.tcf.team/blog/crowdfunding-in-2025). Creators pay for certainty.
first_30_days: Scrape live and recently funded tabletop and hardware campaigns whose updates mention "tariff" or "surcharge", and build a free public teardown of 20 of them (estimated landed cost vs price). Cold-email each creator their own teardown with an offer to run the real audit for $750. Partner with one customs broker for HTS review and one pledge-manager consultant for referrals. Close 5 paid audits and productise the recurring spreadsheet logic into a simple web form.

title: Cross-Lab Calibration Plates for AI Training Data
one_liner: Ready-to-run reference plates and normalization software that make data from different labs, robots and cloud labs comparable enough to train models on.
customer: AI drug-discovery companies that merge internal, CRO and cloud-lab data, high-content screening groups, and cloud labs and CROs that want certified comparability.
problem: Trend chain: autonomous labs, cloud labs and philanthropic data programs multiply data streams. Models then cannot separate batch from biology. The JUMP Cell Painting consortium needed a 302-compound positive-control plate on every batch across 13 sites, and a cross-site organoid study found 2,188 differentially expressed genes by day 84. Physical reference standards for functional assays are not commercially supplied.
solution: Ship 'Reference Plate v1': lot-certified frozen reference cells (a defined iPSC-derived line at a fixed passage), the open JUMP-Target compound set, spike-ins and controls, all pre-plated. Customers run it on every batch. SaaS returns per-plate correction vectors, drift alarms and a 'harmonized to Reference v1' certificate. Expand to viability, high-content imaging and scRNA-seq perturbation assays.
why_now: Lila, Medra, Transfyr and other autonomous-lab efforts are producing data at scale. The OpenAI Foundation's $1B Public Data for Health grants will fund data generation whose cross-site comparability nobody audits. Batch-correction methods are mature, but no shared physical standard exists.
revenue_model: $250-600 per plate, $2-6k/month software, and $10-30k certification audits for labs and CROs.
non_obvious_insight: ERCC spike-ins and NIST-style standards made genomics data poolable. Functional assays lack an equivalent. Standards are winner-take-most: the first plate adopted by three or four major datasets becomes the de facto unit. Physical lots are also a moat that software-only AI shops cannot copy.
first_30_days: Source the JUMP-Target compound set. Produce 200 pilot plates. Give them free to 5 AI startups and cloud labs for a cross-site comparison. Publish the batch-variance reduction and convert the users to paid.

title: Tell Us Once: US Death-Event Switchboard
one_liner: Verify an executor once, then let agents notify and close dozens of institutions for you, building toward a reusable 'authority to act' credential the institutions accept.
customer: Executors and surviving families pay, with distribution through funeral homes, estate attorneys and employers or insurers. Institutions later pay per verified case.
problem: US executors call dozens of banks, card issuers, utilities and subscription companies, each demanding its own certified death certificate, letters and forms. The deceased's identity is exposed to fraud. The UK has 'Tell Us Once', the US has nothing, and the brief finds no dominant software owner of the estate close-out workflow.
solution: The executor uploads the death certificate, ID and letters. The system verifies them once, then voice and browser agents run institution-specific playbooks: credit bureau alerts, identity locks, marketing suppression, subscription and utility cancellations or transfers, date-of-death balance requests and claim forms. A status board tracks every account, and human ops handle exceptions. Over time it issues a verified executor credential institutions accept by API.
why_now: Voice agents that navigate phone trees and hold queues, and browser agents that complete web forms, reached usable reliability in 2025-26. Digital ID wallets are spreading. Insurer and employer channels such as Empathy (50M+ covered policyholders) show buyers for bereavement services, but Empathy is not a close-out execution layer.
revenue_model: $199-$399 flat per estate ($99 wholesale to funeral homes), $10-$40 per verified case from institutions, and insurer or employer benefit contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is repeated verification, not the work itself. A reusable, verified authority credential collapses 60 identical fights into one and gives institutions a fraud-reduction reason to cooperate.
first_30_days: Build playbooks for the top 30 institutions (big banks, card issuers, brokers, telecoms, streaming, credit bureaus). Sell 25 human-in-the-loop cases through 5 funeral homes at $149. Record each institution's requirements to build the data moat.

title: Weaver Ant Crews for Cashew and Mango Orchards
one_liner: Orchard pest control by living ant colonies: trained local 'ant agents' seed, feed and maintain weaver ants in smallholder cashew and mango trees, and the farmers get paid a residue-free premium.
customer: Smallholder cashew and mango cooperatives in Vietnam, Tanzania and West Africa, and the processors and exporters who need residue-free nuts and fruit.
problem: Smallholders spray expensive pesticides to fight coconut bugs, mirids and thrips. Costs are high, farmer health suffers, and exporters worry about residue limits. Biological control from imported predators is out of reach for smallholders.
solution: Weaver ants (Oecophylla smaragdina and O. longinoda) are territorial predators that guard trees against most pests. Our agents seed colonies, connect tree crowns with rope bridges, and supply sugar and protein supplements in the dry season. Cooperatives sign a per-tree, per-season contract. A phone-based check of nest counts and canopy occupancy generates a verified 'pesticide-free days' record that supports premium pricing with buyers.
why_now: Field research already supports it. In Vietnamese mixed pomelo and orange plantations, lower costs from ant treatments produced profit gains of 47% over pesticide plots. Economic studies of African weaver ants exist for Tanzanian cashew, and Vietnamese cashew smallholders (more than 200,000 households) are pesticide-dependent. What is new is cheap phone-based computer vision to verify colony presence, and buyers tightening residue limits.
revenue_model: A per-tree, per-season service fee set below current spray spend, plus a share (for example 10-15%) of any quality or premium uplift negotiated with exporters. Buyers can also pay a per-tonne residue-free supply fee. Ant-agent franchises would scale the model through local micro-entrepreneurs.
non_obvious_insight: Weaver ants were the world's first documented biocontrol, used in Chinese citrus groves for about 1,700 years. They never scaled because no one can patent or sell a colony, so there was no way to capture the value. The business is not the ant; it is the service wrapper, the verification data and the offtake contract that let someone get paid for a free natural crew.
first_30_days: Sign one cooperative in a cashew belt (Binh Phuoc in Vietnam or Mtwara in Tanzania). Recruit and train 20 farmers and 3 ant agents. Seed 500 trees in a pilot and compare pesticide spend and nut quality on matched control rows. Ask one processor to pre-commit to a residue-free premium.

title: Exchange for Unused Grid Interconnection Headroom
one_liner: A market where owners of unused interconnection capacity and stalled queue positions sell time-sliced access to batteries and data centers that cannot wait for the queue.
customer: Sellers: owners of operating solar and wind plants whose interconnection is sized for peaks they hit only some hours a year, holders of stalled or zombie queue positions, and retiring plants holding transferable capacity rights. Buyers: battery developers, data-center developers and large electrifying industrials that need MW-scale grid access in under 24 months.
problem: Queues hold thousands of GW while data centers and storage developers wait years. Existing owners have real headroom and completed studies but no idea what they are worth or how to transfer them under FERC rules, so deals happen only through informal broker phone calls.
solution: Standardized listings: point of interconnection, headroom by hour profile (from public settlement and EIA data), completed studies and network-upgrade dollars already paid, and rule pathway (surplus interconnection service, co-location, capacity-right transfers). The platform screens deals, supports escrowed contracts and builds price discovery in $/kW-year. Later it offers time-sliced flexible contracts, for example a battery using a solar plant's line at night.
why_now: AI-driven load growth is hitting interconnection scarcity in 2026. FERC has pushed surplus and flexible interconnection, ISOs allow some capacity-right transfers, and hourly injection data makes headroom measurable for the first time.
revenue_model: 2% to 4% success fee on contract value, seller SaaS for asset managers ($1k to $3k a month for headroom analytics), and buyer-side search retainers.
non_obvious_insight: The valuable asset is not the megawatt slot; it is the completed study and network upgrades already paid for by an earlier owner, which cut years off the timeline. Most owners do not know their headroom is worth anything.
first_30_days: Use EIA and ISO settlement data plus queue files to find 150 solar plants with low peak utilization. Cold-contact 40 asset managers, sign one exclusive listing, and take a term-sheet conversation to 15 storage and data-center developers. Target one small (about 20 MW) deal for the first success fee.

title: 911 Dispatch Layer for Autonomous Fleets
one_liner: A RapidSOS-style shared layer inside police and fire dispatch tools that lets first responders instantly direct, reach and cite any autonomous vehicle, truck, delivery robot or drone fleet.
customer: Autonomous fleets pay per vehicle (Zoox, May Mobility, Avride, Beep, Gatik, Kodiak, Bot Auto, sidewalk-robot and drone operators). It is free to 911 centers and agencies.
problem: NHTSA sent a first-responder letter on Jul 8, 2026, and fleets rely on small remote-assistance desks (Waymo has about 70 agents on shift, with two centers in the Philippines). Every fleet has its own phone number and process, and driverless trucks have no one to talk to an inspector, since CVSA enhanced-inspection clearance lasts 24 hours and needs a trained inspector. State rules (Texas SB 2807 and California AB 1777, in effect from July 2026, verify) require emergency plans and fast compliance with geofence directives. Dispatchers have about 40 seconds and no unified tool.
solution: An add-in for dispatch systems (plus SMS and web fallback) and a fleet-side API providing geofence and closure directives with acknowledgment and a timestamped compliance receipt for the city. It also gives one-tap lookup by plate, VIN or fleet ID to a live human on that fleet's ops desk, intake and routing of 'notice of noncompliance' citations, a driverless-truck inspection scheduling module, and audit logs for regulators, with responder training cards and drills.
why_now: The state laws just took effect, fleets are multiplying (Waymo across 10-14 metros, Zoox charging fares, Tesla unsupervised in Texas and Florida, Aurora at 200 driverless trucks), and NHTSA is now actively engaging. Prior compliance tools (PrePass/Kodiak) cover only Texas and Louisiana.
revenue_model: $10-25 per vehicle per month plus a $25-60k onboarding fee per fleet, with optional municipal modules for citation processing and drills.
non_obvious_insight: The legal burden lands on fleets, but the user is a dispatcher with seconds, so you win by embedding in tools police already use and giving it away to agencies, as RapidSOS did. Fleets will pay because one standard is cheaper than hundreds of city-by-city integrations.
first_30_days: Interview 20 dispatchers and fire chiefs in Phoenix, Austin and Atlanta. Build a simple web and SMS directive-and-ack tool. Sign one mid-size fleet to a 90-day paid pilot and join the APCO/NENA standards working groups.

title: Supplier Divorce Protection: Tool Census and Overrun Forensics
one_liner: When a US manufacturer leaves a Chinese contract manufacturer, we find out which molds and dies it really owns, and prove whether the ex-supplier is still running them off the books.
customer: US OEMs and PE-owned manufacturers ($50M-$500M revenue) that moved or are moving injection-molded, die-cast, stamped or extruded product out of China within the last 24 months, and hold $200k-$5M of tooling there. The buyer is the COO or VP Supply Chain, with General Counsel as co-signer. General counsel and brand-protection managers are the second buyer.
problem: Most small and mid-size OEMs cannot say which tools they own, where they physically sit, or what condition they are in. The paper trail is a PO line item from 2016 and a WeChat thread. When the relationship ends, the supplier slow-walks tool release, demands storage or release fees, and sometimes runs overruns on your tooling on a third shift and sells them to distributors and marketplaces at a discount. You then compete against your own product, and lawyers cannot help because nobody can prove which tool made which part.
solution: Three stacked products. (1) Tool Census: a local partner audits each supplier on video and in person, laser-tags every tool with a serial, records its condition and appraised value, and captures a macro-photo 'fingerprint' library of each cavity (gate vestige, ejector-pin witness marks, texture flaws, parting-line signature). (2) Overrun Watch: monitor Amazon, Alibaba, 1688, Temu, eBay and Walmart Marketplace for look-alike parts, buy samples, and match them to cavity fingerprints, date wheels and lot codes with computer-vision-assisted forensics. That yields evidence packs for marketplace takedowns, CBP IPR recordation, or counsel. (3) Tool Extraction: negotiate release, handle Chinese export paperwork and freight, and re-qualify the tool in Ohio.
why_now: The Reshoring Initiative's 2026 survey shows 36% of OEMs reshored this year, up from 29%. The 2025 tariff whiplash ended a lot of Chinese supplier relationships, and the Feb 2026 Supreme Court IEEPA ruling is now churning sourcing decisions again, so the number of messy breakups is at a peak. Cheap macro-imaging and vision models make tool-mark matching, previously an expensive forensic-lab exercise, feasible at SMB prices.
revenue_model: Tool Census at $6k-$15k per supplier site. Overrun Watch at $2k-$5k per month per product family. Forensic evidence pack at $3k-$8k per case. Extraction at 8-12% of appraised tool value plus pass-through freight. Expected first-year ACV per client is $40k-$120k.
non_obvious_insight: Outsiders think IP loss in China means someone copies your design. Insiders know the far bigger leak is your own paid-for tool running unrecorded shifts, and that every cavity is a physical fingerprint the supplier cannot deny. Ownership of the tooling is the real leverage in any break-up, and almost nobody documents it until the day they need it.
first_30_days: Skip China operations at first. Sell a remote $2,500 'Marketplace Overrun Audit': buy 10 units of the client's product from 1688, Alibaba and Temu, compare them to the golden sample and lot codes, and deliver a one-page verdict. Sign 3 design partners through Ohio plant-manager and Reshoring Initiative networks, and line up a Dongguan or Ningbo audit contractor by referral. Book a one-hour consult with an IP litigator who will white-label the evidence-pack format.

title: Compliance Runtime and Audit for AI Wellness Apps
one_liner: One API that applies each state's rules for companion and wellness chatbots by user location, logs the evidence, and produces the audit reports regulators and insurers ask for.
customer: Developers of AI companion, coaching, journaling and wellness apps (thousands, mostly under 50 staff), paying $1,500-6,000 a month plus $10-25k for annual audits.
problem: Illinois banned AI in therapeutic roles (Aug 2025). California SB 243 requires AI disclosure, suicide-ideation protocols, break reminders for minors and annual reporting to the Office of Suicide Prevention from July 2027. New York, Nevada and Utah each differ. China has proposed mandatory human handoff and audits. Trump's EO 14365 seeks preemption but is contested. Pennsylvania sued over bots claiming medical licenses. Small teams cannot track this.
solution: An SDK or proxy between app and model with a geo-aware rules engine (disclosures, minor protections, banned claims, crisis protocol), a quarterly red-team and sycophancy/crisis-handoff test suite reviewed by a clinician panel, immutable logs, and auto-generated regulator and insurer reports. A clinician-signed audit letter is the certification.
why_now: SB 243 took effect in Jan 2026, first enforcement landed in May 2026, and preemption fights make the future patchwork unpredictable. Raine and similar suits make insurers and enterprise buyers ask for evidence of safeguards.
revenue_model: SaaS priced by monthly active users, annual audit fee, and per-report fees. Enterprise tier for platforms that host third-party wellness bots.
non_obvious_insight: Preemption uncertainty is a feature. Nobody will hard-code a compliance posture that may flip in 12 months, so a rules-as-configuration layer with evidentiary logs is the durable asset, not any single law.
first_30_days: Build a counsel-reviewed rulebook for CA, NY, IL, NV, UT, PA and the China draft. Scan 100 app-store companion and wellness apps for gaps and email personalized gap reports. Sell five audits at about $5k each.

title: AI-Off Proficiency Checks for Clinicians
one_liner: E.M. Forster's The Machine Stops and Asimov's The Feeling of Power turned into recurrent, pilot-style checks that measure whether clinicians still perform well when the AI is switched off.
customer: GI and radiology group practices, hospital medical staff offices (ongoing professional practice evaluation and credentialing), physician-owned malpractice carriers seeking premium-credit evidence, and residency programs.
problem: Routine AI assistance may erode unaided skill. A 2025 Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology study of 19 experienced endoscopists in Poland found adenoma detection in non-AI colonoscopies fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after AI exposure (the study is observational and has been contested). No one measures unaided proficiency, unlike pilots' manual-flying currency, and outages or out-of-distribution cases will expose the gap.
solution: A quarterly, 25-minute, blinded and timed case set (videos and images with expert ground truth) delivered with AI overlays disabled. Scores are benchmarked against each clinician's own baseline and peer cohort, with drift alerts, targeted micro-drills, and a certificate for credentialing files and insurers. Add an AI-outage drill for departments (tabletop plus live). Start with colonoscopy, then extend to mammography and other AI-assisted reads.
why_now: AI computer-aided detection is now routine in colonoscopy and mammography. The deskilling study made the risk concrete and quotable. Malpractice carriers and hospital counsel are looking for defensible evidence, and the Joint Commission already requires ongoing professional practice evaluation.
revenue_model: $600-1,500 per clinician per year, carrier-funded programs paid per insured group, and enterprise licenses for health systems.
non_obvious_insight: Sell it as insurance evidence and credentialing paperwork, not education. Aviation shows regulators and insurers accept currency requirements once a failure mode is measured. The pre- and post-adoption unaided performance record is also what a hospital will need to defend an AI-related malpractice case, so buyers are motivated to start their baseline now.
first_30_days: License public polyp-video datasets and recruit two GI academic advisors to write ground truth. Build 10 case sets and pilot free for eight weeks with two GI groups. Pitch one physician-owned malpractice carrier on a premium credit for participating groups, then charge about $900 per clinician per year.

title: Revocation List for Leaked ID Documents
one_liner: A neutral, hashed registry of compromised license and passport records that every verifier can check, forcing step-up on IDs from the Nexus/IDScan.net dump.
customer: IDV and KYC vendors, marketplaces, gig platforms, neobanks, telecom and car-rental retail, and lenders, buying an API.
problem: On Aug 31 2026 the Nexus market began selling 153M+ US and Canadian driver's licenses, each with six images including infrared and ultraviolet scans. Researchers call stored ID images 'permanent fraud tools'. Verifiers cannot tell a fresh scan from a leaked record, and issuers will not revoke tens of millions of licenses.
solution: Ingest breach corpora only through controlled, lawful channels (researcher and law-enforcement partners, hash-only contributions). Compute privacy-preserving fingerprints (salted hashes of document number, state and DOB combinations, and perceptual hashes of portraits). Expose an API answering 'has this document instance been seen compromised?' with a risk tier and recommended step-up (mobile ID, bank-account link, in-person). Add hash-prefix consumer lookup and DMV reissue guidance.
why_now: The Nexus dump is the biggest leak of ID scans and follows 2025 leaks of ID photos from age-verification and support systems (e.g., Discord's vendor). Document-image KYC now needs a compensating signal, and verifiers have none.
revenue_model: $0.01-0.05 per check or $2-20K per month subscriptions, with consumer-alert partnerships through banks.
non_obvious_insight: Public-key infrastructure solved 'a trusted key was stolen' with revocation lists, not by preventing theft. Issuers will not revoke documents, but verifiers can pool what they know. The leak itself is the data source, and the value comes from the shared list.
first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 breach researchers and one small IDV vendor. Build the hashing pipeline and API, and clear the design with privacy counsel. Give it free to 10 verifiers, then convert by usage.

title: Right-Size Rx: Deprescribing After GLP-1 Starts
one_liner: Pharmacist outreach that adjusts insulin, sulfonylureas and BP meds in the weeks after a GLP-1 start, sold to payers on avoided harm and drug spend.
customer: Medicare Advantage plans, Medicaid MCOs, ACOs and self-funded employers with large diabetic and hypertensive populations.
problem: Tirzepatide trial protocols recommend cutting sulfonylureas by at least 50% and basal insulin by at least 20% at start, because GLP-1 weight loss lowers glucose and blood pressure. In real practice nobody is triggered or paid to do this, so patients face hypoglycemia, hypotension and falls, while brand diabetes drugs (SGLT2s, DPP-4s) keep getting refilled.
solution: Claims-triggered (and pharmacy-partner-triggered for cash-pay fills) pharmacist outreach at days 7-28 after first fill among patients on insulin, SU or antihypertensives. Collaborative-practice protocols to adjust or recommend changes, home BP and CGM review, and a savings and safety ledger for the payer.
why_now: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge started Jul 1, 2026 and cash pills at $149-$299 are pushing GLP-1s into older, more medicated patients. Payers are fixated on the GLP-1 price line and are missing the neighboring drug lines.
revenue_model: $2-4 per targeted member per month, or $250 per completed episode, plus a share of measurable avoided ED visits and drug savings.
non_obvious_insight: The near-term safety and cost of GLP-1s sits in the other drugs on the patient's list. Payers can offset part of the GLP-1 cost by trimming those, so it belongs on a CFO's line item, not just a quality dashboard.
first_30_days: Approach one regional MA plan or IPA and one pharmacist group. Run a 90-day pilot on 300 patients identified from Rx claims. Measure interventions made, hypoglycemia events and avoided fills, and hand back a savings ledger.

title: Collateral Condition Reports for Farm Equipment
one_liner: Use newly opened Deere diagnostics to certify used-equipment condition for lenders and auctioneers handling a farm-distress wave.
customer: Community ag banks, Farm Credit associations, equipment auction houses and receivers.
problem: Farm bankruptcies are up 19% and row crops face a fourth loss-making year, so lenders are inheriting machinery they cannot value; poor condition data drives lowball auctions.
solution: An inspection product that reads fault history, engine and hydraulic hours and software status through independent diagnostic tools and issues a per-unit condition certificate, then builds valuation comps.
why_now: Deere's $99M settlement obliges it to open diagnostic and repair tools for 10 years, and repair restrictions cost farmers about $4.2B a year, so independent access is finally legitimate.
revenue_model: $250-600 per report, with annual subscriptions for lenders and per-lot fees from auction houses.
non_obvious_insight: Right-to-repair is framed as a farmer-savings story, but its most bankable use is collateral valuation for the lenders and auctioneers who must price distress.
first_30_days: Partner with three Midwest auction houses and two community banks, run 20 paid inspections using existing independent diagnostic tools, and publish sale-price comparisons.

title: Lights-Out Receiving Network for Driverless Freight
one_liner: On-demand night-shift dock crews plus remotely operable gates and dock doors so driverless trucks arriving at 3 a.m. actually get inspected and unloaded.
customer: Driverless-truck operators and their shipper and receiver customers, distribution centers with thin overnight staffing, and brokers offering autonomous lanes.
problem: Driverless trucks run around the clock, but most receivers have no dock labor, yard checks or inspectors at night. The CVSA enhanced-inspection clearance lasts 24 hours and requires a trained inspector, and hub-to-hub handoffs leave 'hundreds of dollars' of human cost per transfer. The PrePass/Kodiak bypass integration is live only in Texas and Louisiana.
solution: Three pieces. First, a network of trained ex-driver and yard-tech turnaround crews for walk-arounds, sensor cleaning and trailer checks. Second, a $3-6k remote gate and dock-door kit so the AV can check in and get a door. Third, on-call unload crews, with everything dispatched from one app and priced per turn below the cost of a human transfer.
why_now: Aurora is exiting 2026 with about 200 driverless trucks and targets 30,000 by 2030, California's driverless-truck rules took effect on April 28, 2026, and the Teamsters sued on August 5. Hiring retrained drivers into new roles also buys political goodwill.
revenue_model: $150-400 per truck turn, equipment lease or subscription for gate and dock kits, and a per-lane subscription for receivers.
non_obvious_insight: Autonomy shifts the constraint from driver hours to dock hours: the truck no longer sleeps, but the receiver does. The rent moves to whoever owns the human touch at the endpoints, and hiring displaced drivers turns opposition into a labor supply.
first_30_days: Pick one corridor where driverless trucks already run (for example Fort Worth to El Paso). Sign LOIs with 2 shippers on that lane for overnight receiving, recruit 10 ex-drivers or yard techs, build a simple dispatch app and target first paid turns within 90 days.

title: Recorded Parent Voices, Endowed to Outlive Us
one_liner: Guided, human-only voice and video milestone messages for the children of dying parents, with the hosting prepaid so the recordings outlive the company.
customer: Terminally ill parents of minor children, or their spouses. Referrals come from oncology and young-adult cancer social workers, child-life specialists, and hospice social workers. Hospice foundations sponsor families who cannot pay.
problem: Dying parents of young children want to leave their actual voice for the 16th birthday, the wedding and the first heartbreak. They start too late. By the time hospice admission happens, many patients are too sedated, breathless or confused to record anything usable. The generic tools (StoryWorth-style prompts, phone voice memos) produce rambling, prompt-less files. Families also do not trust vendors to still exist in 20 years. Meanwhile AI voice-cloning 'deadbots' are being pitched at the same families, and most of them recoil.
solution: A two-session guided capture (in person or on video) run by a trained 'legacy guide' with a chaplain or child-bereavement background. It uses a prompt library organized by the child's future age: what a 12-year-old needs to hear versus a 30-year-old. Examples: 'how I met your dad', 'what I was afraid of', 'what I'd say when you're furious at me', and a mundane category (how I laughed, my opinion of your first crush) that grown children say matters most. The output is edited, human-only audio and video with a strict no-synthesis policy. Each message is tagged to a milestone and delivered by the surviving guardian's app. There is a physical archival copy and printed transcripts. Hosting is prepaid into a trust-held reserve, with a contractual right to export everything if the company dies. Durability and authenticity are the product, not features.
why_now: AI voice-cloning is now cheap and good enough that grief-tech is being flooded with synthetic 'talk to your dead mom' products. Public and clinical unease about them is rising, which opens a clear 'only what they actually said' position. At least some early digital-afterlife vendors have folded or pivoted, so buyers are primed to ask 'will this exist in 2045?'. Phone-quality recording is now good enough that no studio is needed. I could not verify specific vendor failures in this session, so confirm before using them in marketing.
revenue_model: Roughly $450 for guided capture plus a one-time $600 to $900 permanence endowment (about $1,000 to $1,400 per family). The endowment funds 30-year hosting, and the reserve is held in a trust or escrow. Add-ons: printed keepsake book, extra milestone messages, and an 'audio blessing' set for each child. Hospice and hospital foundations sponsor uninsured families at a discounted wholesale rate.
non_obvious_insight: The market timing is wrong in everyone's mind. The recording window closes weeks before hospice, so the referral source is oncology, not hospice. What dying parents fear most is not death but vanishing, and that includes the file vanishing. Buyers will pay more for a credible 'this outlives our company' promise than for any feature. Refusing to synthesize is a selling point that families and chaplains will repeat.
first_30_days: Recruit two oncology or child-life social workers as design partners. Run 8 to 10 free pilot sessions using a phone and a $60 lavalier mic, and write the age-banded prompt library from what the kids' guardians say they'd want. Get a small-estates attorney or trust company to set up the escrow and export-if-we-fail clause. Put up a one-page site, then charge from case 11. Ask the first families for a written testimonial and referrals to two other oncology units.

title: Recovering Tariff Surcharges Small Buyers Already Paid
one_liner: Contingency-fee forensic audits of supplier invoices that find the explicit 'tariff surcharge' lines small retailers, contractors and restaurants paid in 2025, and turn them into evidence packets while importers hold the refund money.
customer: Small retailers, contractors, restaurants, salons and small manufacturers that bought from distributors who itemized tariff surcharges. Fee is about 25% of recovery. Secondary customers are mid-size distributors that received IEEPA refunds and want a defensible pass-through rebate calculation.
problem: The Supreme Court ruled on 2026-02-20 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs. CBP says about $166B is refundable to 330,000+ importers of record, with about $81B paid by July 2026. 76% of firms that source internationally passed costs to customers, so downstream small buyers paid the tax and get nothing directly (brief inference). Brokers and trade lawyers chase the importer's refund, not the payer's claim.
solution: The owner forwards a supplier-invoice mailbox or QuickBooks export. Document AI extracts surcharge lines and products, identifies the likely importer of record, calculates the claim, and packages evidence (invoice, surcharge wording, date, refund status) into a demand letter. A partner consumer-protection or commercial firm handles aggregated claims and arbitration. Distributors get an audit-trailed rebate module for voluntary pass-through.
why_now: The refund flow is happening now (CAPE launched by April 2026, 2,000+ suits filed), importers hold the cash, and downstream invoice records and claim windows decay every month. Document AI makes invoice-level extraction cheap. The IEEPA ruling is a one-time event, so the window is finite.
revenue_model: 25% contingency on recovered amounts, split with counsel. Add SaaS fees from distributors for rebate audits.
non_obvious_insight: Explicit surcharge line items are invoice-level admissions that the charge existed to cover a tax later refunded, which makes these claims far stronger than generic price-increase complaints. Distributors want to keep small customers, so a clean evidence packet often converts to a negotiated credit without litigation. Claim strength varies by contract and state and needs counsel, so the business is forensic evidence assembly, not legal advice.
first_30_days: Build the invoice parser on 50 sample invoices and offer free surcharge scans to 30 members of one trade association (independent hardware, bike or restaurant-supply buyers). Identify the 10 most frequent surcharging distributors, sign a contingency-split agreement with a law firm, and target first negotiated credits by month 3.

title: Inverter-Telemetry Credit Bureau for African Solar
one_liner: Turn the cloud data that hybrid inverters and batteries already stream into a consented energy cash-flow score, so lenders, insurers and installers can finance an asset boom that official statistics cannot see.
customer: Solar and battery asset financiers, MFIs and banks in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, plus installers who need financing to close sales. Insurers and DFIs paying for verified performance come later.
problem: Africa installs 17 GW of solar in 2026 (+45%), 75% of the growth is distributed, and it imports more battery dollars than panels. Ember says its estimates are 2x official figures and only 14 of 54 countries reported 2025 data, so credit bureaus and insurers have nothing to price on. Installers cannot get customers financed, and lenders cannot see collateral health or borrower activity.
solution: With owner consent gathered through the installer, pull production, load, battery health, uptime and location data from inverter and BMS clouds (Victron VRM, Solarman for Deye, Growatt, Huawei, Solis). Compute diesel displacement and savings, a load-profile proxy for business activity (cold-room cycles, salon hours), collateral health and tamper flags, and installer quality scores. Sell an API and dashboard to lenders, with remote-lock hooks and insurer feeds as add-ons.
why_now: Distributed solar plus batteries has become private infrastructure. Stationary packs fell 45% to about $70/kWh, African equity funding is concentrated while debt replaces equity (so lenders need collateral visibility), and India's UPI fee change shows how fragile transaction-data underwriting is. The US also needs neutral telemetry, since Sunrun and Tesla's 16.8 GW capacity-as-a-service has no disclosed verification standard.
revenue_model: $2-6 per scored asset per month or per-report fees, a 1-2% origination fee on financing it unlocks, installer SaaS, insurer data licensing, and later verification fees from results-based financing programs.
non_obvious_insight: The best alternative-credit dataset in Africa is already being emitted by hardware nobody thinks of as a bureau. Energy consumption is a real-time proxy for small-business activity, and the inverter is both the collateral and the sensor. Because the data layer is vendor-neutral, it can later certify firm distributed capacity for utilities and hyperscalers, something Tesla and Enphase cannot credibly do for each other's fleets.
first_30_days: Integrate two APIs (Victron VRM and Solarman/Deye) and sign 3 installers in Lagos, Nairobi or Johannesburg with 300+ systems between them. Collect customer consents through the installers' apps and publish a free installed-base map. Take the top-scoring 30 customers to one MFI or asset financier for a pilot loan pool, charging a 2% origination fee.

title: Idle Brewery Tanks as Biotech Pilot Plants
one_liner: Retrofit closing or underused craft breweries into shared 200 to 2,000 liter fermentation pilot plants for food-ingredient, cosmetic-ingredient and biomaterial startups.
customer: Pre-seed to Series A synthetic-biology and food-tech startups that need samples, regulatory batches and customer trials at pilot scale, plus struggling brewery owners who get rent or revenue share.
problem: Startups can make grams in the lab but face a valley before contract manufacturers will touch them: schedules booked, minimums high, and building their own plant is slow. Pilot-scale fermentation capacity is a widely reported gap. Meanwhile craft brewers are closing: 481 closures against 300 openings in 2025, and 9,344 breweries operating in June 2026, down 1.8% year over year.
solution: A 'bio-foundry co-op'. Lease off-hours tank time from 1 to 3 breweries. Add a portable sterile-air skid, in-place cleaning and sterilization protocols, a single-use inoculum train, and harvest and dewatering equipment (decanter or centrifuge, with drying done through mobile partners). Start with well-characterized yeast (Saccharomyces, Pichia) and other low-risk hosts. Sell fixed-price run packages, with brewer-trained operators supervised by a process scientist.
why_now: Breweries are stranded with stainless tanks, utilities, trade-waste permits and skilled operators, while beer volume keeps shrinking. Food and materials biotech has more strains than pilot capacity. The gap is at 500 to 2,000 liters, not 100,000, and that is exactly brewery scale.
revenue_model: Per-run fees ($8k to $25k), tech-transfer and process-development fees, a rent or revenue share to the brewery, and later a multi-year reserved-capacity subscription for repeat customers.
non_obvious_insight: The moat isn't the tank, it's the permitting: zoning, industrial wastewater discharge capacity for high-BOD effluent, food-grade utilities and a building already approved for fermentation take biotech companies years to secure. Breweries have all of it. Brewers are also the biggest pool of people who instinctively know how to keep yeast at scale contamination-free.
first_30_days: Sign a letter of intent with one distressed brewery on an off-hours share. Recruit 3 startups from synbio and food-tech directories and sell a paid $5k to $10k feasibility run at 200 liters. Prepare a biosafety plan and speak to the local wastewater authority early. Line up a part-time process scientist.

title: Sewershed Chemical Fingerprinting to Trace PFAS Sources
one_liner: A network of automated samplers plus non-target mass-spectrometry that bisects a city's sewer tree to find which industrial sources are putting PFAS into the plant.
customer: Wastewater utilities with biosolids or effluent PFAS problems, industrial pretreatment coordinators, state PFAS programs (Michigan's industrial pretreatment PFAS initiative is a precedent, from my background knowledge), and industrial dischargers that want an independent baseline. The utility or state pays.
problem: Wastewater plants cannot remove PFAS, yet they receive it from platers, landfills, textile, paper and semiconductor users, and they inherit the biosolids and effluent liability. Utilities treat sources as unknowable, so they cannot enforce or recover cost. Europe's polluter-pays wastewater rules will also need load attribution.
solution: Install 10-30 autosamplers per sewershed (pump stations and manholes). Analyze weekly composites through a partner lab using high-resolution mass spectrometry, total organofluorine and precursor assays. Use ML on the network tree to attribute loads to upstream sub-catchments, then deliver a source map and enforcement-grade evidence. First product: a 12-week campaign.
why_now: The 2027 monitoring wave, biosolids scrutiny, and falling costs of high-resolution mass spectrometry plus the COVID-era playbook for sewer-network sampling all converge.
revenue_model: $120-300k per campaign, $60-150k/yr surveillance subscriptions, and cost-recovery success fees.
non_obvious_insight: A sewer network is a tree, so 15 samplers can bisect to a source in weeks, like contact tracing. The buyer is the utility's legal and finance side seeking cost recovery from polluters, not the environmental regulator.
first_30_days: Sign one small city or regional plant with a known biosolids problem, or a state program. Partner with a commercial lab that has non-target capability instead of buying instruments. Run a pilot at eight nodes and produce a source-bisection map.
